# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.
I'll explore the codebase to locate the transaction-categorization enrichment logic and the fixtures behind these RC 2.14 findings.

# Transaction Categorization / Enrichment — Codebase Report

## 1. Overall project structure

**Stack:** Python 3.9 Flask microservice (`categorizationapp`), pandas rule engine, Docker + gunicorn on port **9898**.

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # python:3.9.2, pip install -e ., gunicorn :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # package deps (Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, …)
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app factory
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP API + bank dispatch + enrichment pipeline
        ├── BankScripts/                # per-bank categorization (35 banks)
        └── UtilityScripts/             # shared rules, enums, name cleaning, salary, PFM
```

**Languages:** Python only. No JS/Java/Go.

**Tests / fixtures:** **None in the repo.** No `tests/`, `pytest`, fixtures, baselines, or RC 2.14 artifacts. Git history is a single commit (`047782b import codebase`). RC 2.14 / F-1…F-5 labels are **not present as files** — they map to behavioral gaps in the live rule code (especially **Canara**, secondarily **HDFC/PNB**).

**How enrichment works (pipeline per bank):**

```
POST /categorizeTransaction
  → AppUtil.clean_input_df
  → BankScripts.<Bank>.categorize_*_transactions   # category + partyName
  → [CC] card_clean_names + card_purpose
  → purpose()                 # subcategory / purpose from RegexConstants
  → clean_names()             # merchant normalization (CleanName.py)
  → internal_payment()        # fuzzy match holder name
  → [SAVING] salary_detection()
  → [optional] pfm_categorization + simple_description
```

**API routes** (`Controller.py`):
- `GET /`
- `POST /categorizeTransaction` — main path
- `POST /recurrentTransactions`

**Core pattern everywhere:** ordered `conditions_choices` lists → `np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")`. **First true condition wins.** Category defaults to `"TRANSFER"`; party defaults to `""`.

---

## 2. Where category & counterparty name are derived

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | Bank switch, full pipeline |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` | **Primary:** `transactionCategory` + `partyName` via regex/`np.select` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` | Splitters: `sep_by_`, `sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_colon`, `py_extract` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | Bank-specific regex (cheque, MICR, ACC_VERIF, NEFT…) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` | Cross-bank purpose/merchant regex (loan, P2P NBFC, salary…) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` | Subcategory (salary, loan, shopping…) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` | Canonical merchant names from `partyName`/`description` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py` / `CardPurpose.py` | Credit-card path |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` | Self-transfer via fuzzywuzzy |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` | Salary clustering |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` | PFM buckets |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SimpleDescription.py` | Human-readable labels |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` | Category enum incl. `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`, `CHEQUE_PAID`, `UPI`, … |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` | Subcategory enum |

**Counterparty field:** `partyName` (display) and `party2` (spaces stripped) set in each bank script.

---

## 3. Cheques, MICR CLG, electronic transfers, P2P, account verification

### Cheques / MICR CLG

**Shared constants** — `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py`:

- `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1`–`10` — MICR CLG / CHQ PAID-INWARD / MICR CTS / etc. (lines ~80–90)
- `CHQ_PATTERN1`–`4` — MICR INWARD / TO CLG (Kotak-style)
- `PNB_CHQ_0`–`8` — `TO TRF` / `TO TR` cheque narratives
- `CHQ_CLEAN`, `CHQ_CLEAN2`, `CHQ_CLEAN_KOTAK`

**Bank scripts with strong cheque rules:**  
`HDFC.py`, `Canara.py`, `PNB.py`, `YES.py`, `UCO.py`, `Axis.py`, `Kotak.py`, `BOB.py`, `BankOfMaharashtra.py`, `IDBI.py`, `UnionBank.py`, `Syndicate.py`, …

**Canara cheque category** (`Canara.py` ~70–71):

```python
to clg|by clg|\bchq\b|cheque  → CHEQUE_DEPOSIT / CHEQUE_PAID
```

**Canara cheque party** (~163–166):

```python
Chq Paid-Home Clearing-  → sep_by_dash(..., 2, 3)   # correct name slot
^CHQ PAID-               → sep_by_dash(..., 1, 2)   # WRONG for MICR CLG
^To Clg :                → colon/dash extract
```

**HDFC** uses `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN*` + later wipe of `Micr Clg|Chq Paid` party names (line 260).

**Bare cheque number in `remark`:** many banks treat `remark ~ ^[0-9]{3,6}$` as cheque; **Canara does not.**

### Electronic transfers (NEFT / RTGS / IMPS / FT)

Per-bank category keywords + slash/dash/colon party parsers. Canara examples (`Canara.py` 58–60, 111–127, 146–156):

- Category: `^NEFT`, `^RTGS`, `MB-IMPS|^IMPS|…`, `funds? xfer`
- Party: `NEFT-` → dash segment 1; `^IMPS:` → **colon segment 1**; `MB-IMPS- CR/` → slash segment 1; `FUNDS TRANSFER FROM` → extract

### Instant payments / P2P (UPI)

- Category: `^UPI|MB-UPI|\bUPV/DR/|…` → `"UPI"` (`Canara.py` 57)
- Party (`Canara.py` 107–109):
  - `^UPI/0` + 7 slashes → last segment
  - `^UPI/[CD]R` → **slash index 2** (often the **RRN**, not name)
  - `UPV/DR/` → index 3
- Cleanup wipes `^[0-9]{5,}` party names → blank after wrong extract
- **Note:** `P2P` in `RegexConstants.py` is **P2P NBFC lenders** (lendbox, monexo…), not UPI P2P person-to-person

### Account verification (penny drop)

Constants: `BANK_VERIF` (Canara), `BANK_VER` (HDFC/Axis/BOM), `ACC_VERIFY_PNB`, `ACC_VERIF` (SBI), etc.

Canara (`Canara.py` 19):

```python
BANK_VERIF & amount.lt(1) → ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION
```

Typical penny-drop is **₹1**, so `amount.lt(1)` **never matches** amount=1. Other banks use `lt(2)`, `eq(1)`, or `isin([1,-1])`.

`BANK_VERIF` also includes broad tokens like `FUND TRANS` and `IMPS Txn` (can mis-fire if amount threshold were fixed carelessly).

---

## 4. Fixtures / baselines for RC 2.14 or F-1…F-5

**Not found.** No files matching RC 2.14, F-1…F-5, baseline, or regression fixtures.

Closest “source of truth” for those findings is the rule logic itself (especially **`Canara.py`**, modified mtime 2026-07-15 vs Nov 2022 for most other banks — possible partial edit surface).

---

## 5. How to run tests / the service

**No automated test suite.** Practical ways to exercise:

```bash
# Install (pinned scipy 1.7.3 may fail on modern Python — relax pins if needed)
cd /app/categorizationapp
pip3 install -e .
# or: pip install Flask pandas numpy fuzzywuzzy python-Levenshtein ...

# Run API
export PYTHONPATH=/app/categorizationapp
python -m categorizationapp
# or: gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app
# Docker: docker build -t te . && docker run -p 9898:9898 te

# Smoke-call
curl -s localhost:9898/categorizeTransaction -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "bank":"CANARA","acc_type":"SAVING","accountUID":"x","accountHolder":"",
  "transactions":[{"description":"CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR","amount":1000,
                   "type":"DEBIT","remark":"","balanceAfterTransaction":5000}]
}'
```

**Direct unit-style call (what I used):**

```python
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Canara import categorize_Canara_transactions
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame([{...}])
categorize_Canara_transactions(df, "SAVING")
```

---

## 6. Findings F-1…F-5 — root causes (verified by running Canara/HDFC/PNB)

All reproduced against current code with `PYTHONPATH=/app/categorizationapp`.

### F-1: Cheque debit with bare number note → generic `TRANSFER`

**Primary:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Canara.py`  
Canara never maps numeric `remark` (cheque number) → `CHEQUE_PAID`.

| Input | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `description=""`, `remark="123456"`, DEBIT | `TRANSFER` |
| `description="RAVI KUMAR"`, `remark="456789"`, DEBIT | `TRANSFER` |

**Contrast (working pattern elsewhere):**  
`YES.py` / `UCO.py` / `Axis.py` / `Kotak.py` / `PNB.py`:

```python
remark ~ ^[0-9]{3,6}$ & DEBIT → CHEQUE_PAID
```

**PNB nuance:** only `^[0-9]{5}$` for debit — 6-digit cheque numbers still become `TRANSFER`.

**Fix direction:** Add Canara (and tighten PNB) remark-based cheque rules, similar to YES/Axis; optionally require empty/non-narrative description to avoid false positives.

---

### F-2: `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → counterparty = clearing tag

**Primary:** `Canara.py` lines 164–165

```python
# Home Clearing: correct — takes segment after second dash
Chq Paid-Home Clearing- → sep_by_dash(desc, 2, 3)  # "RAVI KUMAR" ✓

# Generic CHQ PAID-: wrong index for MICR CLG
^CHQ PAID- → sep_by_dash(desc, 1, 2)  # "MICR CLG" ✗
```

**Reproduced:**

| Description | Category | partyName |
|-------------|----------|-----------|
| `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` | `CHEQUE_PAID` | **`Micr Clg`** |
| `CHQ PAID-MICR CTS-RAVI KUMAR` | `CHEQUE_PAID` | **`Micr Cts`** |
| `CHQ PAID-INWARD-RAVI KUMAR` | `CHEQUE_PAID` | **`Inward`** |
| `Chq Paid-Home Clearing-RAVI KUMAR` | `CHEQUE_PAID` | `Ravi Kumar` ✓ |

**HDFC related bug:** `CHQ PAID-` uses `sep_by_dash(..., 3, 4)` (empty for 3-part strings) then blanks `Micr Clg|Chq Paid` → category OK, **party empty** (loses “RAVI KUMAR”). `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6` only covers `MICR CTS`, not `MICR CLG`.

**Fix direction:** For `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-NAME` / `MICR CTS-NAME` / `INWARD-NAME`, take the **last** dash segment (or add dedicated patterns like Home Clearing). Strip internal tags `MICR CLG|MICR CTS|INWARD|TRANSFER` from party.

---

### F-3: Inbound electronic-transfer credits → blank counterparty

**Primary:** `Canara.py` IMPS/NEFT party rules + digit cleanup (lines 123–127, 174).

```python
^IMPS: → sep_by_colon(desc, 1, 2)   # often RRN when format is IMPS:RRN:NAME
# then:
partyName ~ ^[0-9]{5,} → ""         # wipes the RRN → blank name
```

**Reproduced:**

| Description | Category | partyName |
|-------------|----------|-----------|
| `IMPS:123456789012:SENDER NAME` | `IMPS` | **`''`** |
| `IMPS:JOHN DOE:123456789012` | `IMPS` | `John Doe` ✓ |
| `IMPS-CREDIT-JOHN DOE-XX1234` | `IMPS` | **`''`** |
| `INB IMPS/CR/JOHN DOE/xx` | `IMPS` | **`''`** |
| `MB-IMPS- CR/SENDER NAME/...` | `IMPS` | `Sender Name` ✓ |

**Fix direction:** Prefer non-numeric colon/slash segments; add `IMPS-CREDIT-` / `INB IMPS/` parsers; when segment 1 is all digits, take segment 2 as name.

---

### F-4: P2P instant-payment (UPI) credit → bare ref / missing sender

**Primary:** `Canara.py` lines 107–109, 174

```python
^UPI/[CD]R → sep_by_(desc, 2, 3)   # UPI/CR/<RRN>/<NAME>/... → RRN at index 2
# cleanup:
^[0-9]{5,} → ""                     # blanks RRN → empty party (or bare RRN if cleanup skipped)
```

**Reproduced:**

| Description | partyName |
|-------------|-----------|
| `UPI/CR/441122334455/RAVI KUMAR/SBIN001/UPI` | **`''`** (extracted RRN then wiped) |
| `UPI/DR/441122334455/RAVI KUMAR/paytm@paytm/Pay` | **`''`** |
| `UPI/441122334455/RAVI KUMAR/SBIN/xxx` | **`''`** (no matching rule) |
| `UPI/0/.../note/extra` (7 slashes) | **`Extra`** (wrong last field) |
| `UPV/DR/123.../BOB SMITH/paytm` | `Bob Smith` ✓ |

**Fix direction:** For `UPI/CR|DR/<rrn>/<name>/...` use **index 3** for name (or first alphabetic slash field). Do not keep pure numeric RRNs as `partyName`.

---

### F-5: Account verification token deposit → ordinary `TRANSFER`

**Primary:** `Canara.py` line 19 + `BANK_VERIF` in `BankRegexConstants.py` line 321

```python
BANK_VERIF & amount.lt(1) → ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION
# ₹1 penny-drop: 1 < 1 is False → falls through to default TRANSFER
```

**Reproduced:**

| Description | amount | Category |
|-------------|--------|----------|
| `Account verification by Google` | 1 | **`TRANSFER`** |
| `PennyDrop validation` | 1 | **`TRANSFER`** |
| `nydrop test` | 1 | **`TRANSFER`** |
| `Account verification` | 0.5 | `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` ✓ |
| HDFC `PennyDrop` | 1 | `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` ✓ (`amount.lt(2)`) |

**Fix direction:** Align with peers: `amount.lt(2)` or `amount.isin([1, -1])` or `amount.le(1)`. Review `BANK_VERIF` breadth (`FUND TRANS`, `IMPS Txn`) so fixing the threshold does not mass-misclassify normal IMPS/FT.

---

## Quick reference — files most relevant to F-1…F-5

| File | Why |
|------|-----|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Canara.py` | **All five findings** concentrated here |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | `BANK_VERIF`, HDFC/PNB cheque & MICR patterns |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py` | MICR CLG / CHQ PAID party loss; good ACC_VER threshold |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/PNB.py` | Partial bare-cheque remark handling (5 digits only) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/YES.py` / `Axis.py` / `UCO.py` | Reference implementations for remark→cheque |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` | `sep_by_*` off-by-index root of F-2/F-3/F-4 |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | `bank == "CANARA"` pipeline (~403) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` | `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`, `CHEQUE_PAID`, `UPI`, … |

---

## Architectural notes

1. **No tests/fixtures** — regression for RC 2.14 would need new cases; none ship with the repo.
2. **Order-sensitive `np.select`** — later, better rules never run if an earlier broad rule matches.
3. **Default `TRANSFER`** — any unmatched narrative becomes a generic transfer (F-1, F-5).
4. **Party extraction is positional** (slash/dash/colon index), not semantic — fragile when banks insert MICR tags or leading RRNs (F-2, F-3, F-4).
5. **`P2P` in Purpose/RegexConstants** = NBFC brand list, not UPI person-to-person.

I can next draft concrete patch diffs for Canara F-1…F-5 (and optional HDFC/PNB follow-ups) if you want that.
